dataset: Gene expression feature matrix (samples x genes) with binary disease_status labels
goal: Train and evaluate a classifier that predicts disease status from expression features, with a trustworthy estimate of generalization performance

seeded_errors.description: StandardScaler is fit on the full feature matrix X (fit_transform on all samples) before the train/test split exists. Test-set statistics (mean, variance per gene) leak into the scaling applied to the training data, inflating apparent performance.
seeded_errors.line_hint: X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X)   # fit on the FULL dataset

seeded_errors.description: Feature selection (SelectKBest) is fit on the full dataset, including the full label vector y, before any train/test split. This lets information about which genes discriminate cases from controls in the test set influence the feature set used for training -- a classic and severe leakage pattern, since the 'test' set was never truly held out from feature selection.
seeded_errors.line_hint: X_selected = selector.fit_transform(X_scaled, y)   # fit on the FULL dataset

seeded_errors.description: train_test_split is called with no random_state (non-reproducible split across runs) and no stratify=y, so class balance between disease and control is not guaranteed to be preserved in either the train or test partition.
seeded_errors.line_hint: X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X_selected, y, test_size=0.25)

seeded_errors.description: Model evaluation is performed on X_train/y_train (the same data the model was fit on) rather than the held-out X_test/y_test. X_test and y_test are created by the split but never used anywhere in the script. The reported accuracy reflects memorization/fit quality, not generalization to unseen samples.

Only plain accuracy is reported. For a disease/control classification task, which is commonly class-imbalanced, accuracy can look high while the model performs poorly on the minority class. No balanced accuracy, ROC-AUC, precision/recall, or confusion matrix is reported, and class balance is never checked or printed.

LogisticRegression is instantiated without class_weight='balanced' (or any other imbalance-handling strategy), and class distribution is never inspected before modeling, compounding the risk that the wrong metric (E5) is masking poor minority-class performance.
